18, 2022|website=FIBA.com|access-date=April 10, 2021}} also known as '''Bruno Fernando'''{{cite web|title=Bruno Fernando {{!}} Atlanta Hawks {{!}} NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/player/1628981/bruno-fernando/rotowire|website=NBA.com|access-date=April 10, 2021}} (born August 15, 1998), is an Angolan professional [[basketball]] player for [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[EuroLeague]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|Maryland Terrapins]]. Fernando is the first NBA player from [[Angola]], and also plays for the [[Angola men's national basketball team|Angola national team]] and won a gold medal at [[AfroBasket 2025]]. ==Early life== A native of [[Luanda]], [[Angola]], Bruno Fernando started playing basketball in his hometown.{{Cite news|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2017/04/07/basketball-grew-quickly-on-maryland-recruit-bruno-fernando/|title=Basketball grew quickly on Maryland recruit Bruno Fernando|last=Markus|first=Don|work=baltimoresun.com|access-date=December 30, 2017|language=en-US|archive-date=October 2, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181002020643/http://www.baltimoresun.com/sports/terps/tracking-the-terps/bs-sp-terps-recruit-bruno-fernando-0408-20170407-story.html|url-status=live}} While playing the [[2014 FIBA Under-17 World Championship]] with the Angolan national team, he caught the eye of scouts in the US. In early 2015, he joined the [[Montverde Academy]] in [[Montverde, Florida]].{{Cite news |last=Stubbs |first=Roman |date=October 2, 2016 |title=Angolan Bruno Fernando becomes Maryland basketball's first commit of 2017 class |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/terrapins-insider/wp/2016/10/02/angolan-bruno-fernando-becomes-maryland-basketballs-first-commit-of-2017-class/ |access-date=December 30, 2017 |newspaper=The Washington Post |language=en-US |issn=0190-8286}} He committed to [[SMU Mustangs men's basketball|Southern Methodist University]] in April 2016{{Cite news|url=https://www.si.com/college-basketball/2016/04/01/smu-bruno-fernando-commits-four-star-center|title=Four-star center Bruno Fernando commits to SMU|work=SI.com|access-date=December 30, 2017|language=en}} but decided the following month to [[reclassification (education)|reclassify]] into the Class of 2017. He spent the 2016–17 season at [[IMG Academy]] in [[Bradenton, Florida]].{{Cite news|url=https://bustingbrackets.com/2016/10/02/maryland-basketball-former-smu-bruno-fernando-chooses-terps/|title=Maryland Basketball: Former SMU Bruno Fernando chooses Terps|date=October 2, 2016|work=Busting Brackets|access-date=December 30, 2017|language=en-US|archive-date=February 25, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200225134754/https://bustingbrackets.com/2016/10/02/maryland-basketball-former-smu-bruno-fernando-chooses-terps/|url-status=dead}} In October 2016, Bruno Fernando committed to the [[Maryland Terrapins men's basketball|University of Maryland]], after also considering [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]], [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]] and [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]], among others.{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/news/terrapins-insider/wp/2016/11/10/maryland-basketball-officially-signs-2017-prospects-bruno-fernando-darryl-morsell/|title=Maryland basketball officially signs 2017 prospects Bruno Fernando, Darryl Morsell|last=Stubbs|first=Roman|date=November 10, 2016|newspaper=Washington Post|access-date=December 30, 2017|language=en-US|issn=0190-8286}} ==College career== Fernando made his debut for Maryland on November 10, 2017, against [[Stony Brook Seawolves men's basketball|Stony Brook]]. Coming off the bench, he scored ten points to go along with two rebounds, one assist, one block and one steal in 13 minutes of playing time.{{Cite web |date=November 10, 2017 |title=Maryland vs Stony Brook (11/10/17 at Nassau Coliseum) |url=https://umterps.com/sports/2018/7/6/2137789.html.aspx#GAME.BOX |access-date=November 25, 2024 |website=umterps.com}} He was named Big Ten Freshman of the Week on January 8, 2018, after posting 17 points and 11 rebounds against [[Penn State Nittany Lions men's basketball|Penn State]] and a career-high 21 points in a 91–73 win versus [[Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball|Iowa]].{{Cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/010818aag.html|title=Maryland, Ohio State Earn Weekly Men's Basketball Honors: Buckeyes' Keita Bates-Diop earns Player of the Week award; Terrapins' Bruno Fernando named Freshman of the Week|website=[[Big Ten Conference]]|language=en|access-date=January 8, 2018|date=January 8, 2018|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180109063608/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/010818aag.html|archive-date=January 9, 2018|url-status=dead}} He had a strong freshman season as he averaged 10.3 points, 6.5 rebounds and 1.2 blocks per game, and earned All-Big Ten Freshman honors. After the season, Fernando declared for the [[2018 NBA draft]] and participated in the [[NBA Draft Combine]] that year, but withdrew from the draft and returned to Maryland.{{cite news |last=Phillips |first=Scott |title=Maryland big man Bruno Fernando withdraws from 2018 NBA Draft |url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2018/05/28/maryland-big-man-bruno-fernando-withdraws-from-2018-nba-draft/ |access-date=May 30, 2018 |work=[[NBC Sports]] |date=May 28, 2018}} ==Professional career== [[File:Bruno Fernando Jordan McRae.jpg|thumb|left|Fernando and [[Jordan McRae]] in 2019]] ===Atlanta Hawks / College Park Skyhawks (2019–2021)=== Fernando was selected as the 34th pick of the [[2019 NBA draft]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. Fernando became the first Angolan player to be selected in the [[NBA draft]].{{cite web |last=Giambalvo |first=Emily |date=June 20, 2019 |title=Maryland's Bruno Fernando drafted 34th overall, will be traded to the Hawks |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/2019/06/21/marylands-bruno-fernando-drafted-th-overall-reportedly-headed-hawks/?noredirect=on |access-date=June 25, 2019 |website=WashingtonPost.com |language=en}} He was traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-acquire-draft-rights-bruno-fernando-76ers|title=Atlanta Hawks Acquire Draft Rights To Bruno Fernando From 76ers|work=NBA.com|date=July 6, 2019}} On July 7, 2019, the Hawks announced that they had signed Fernando.{{cite web |last=Finberg |first=Annie |date=July 7, 2019 |title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Bruno Fernando |url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-bruno-fernando |access-date=July 7, 2019 |work=NBA.com}} On October 24, 2019, Fernando made his debut in NBA, coming off from bench in a 117–100 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]] with seven points, three rebounds and two assists.{{cite web |date=October 24, 2019 |title=Trae Young has 38 points, Hawks beat Pistons 117-110 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401160656 |access-date=October 24, 2019 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press}} He received his first assignment to the Hawks' [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[College Park Skyhawks]], on November 25. He made his G League debut that evening. Fernando missed several games in January 2020 due to the death of his mother.{{cite news |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/hawks-bruno-fernando-remains-out-tuesday/ |title=Hawks' Bruno Fernando: Remains out Tuesday |access-date=January 13, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 13, 2020}} On June 20, 2021, Fernando was suspended for one game without pay for leaving the bench during an altercation between the Hawks and the [[Philadelphia 76ers]].{{Cite web |date=June 20, 2021 |title=Hawks' Bruno Fernando suspended and 76ers' Joel Embiid fined |url=https://pr.nba.com/bruno-fernando-joel-embiid-altercation/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211011025425/https://pr.nba.com/bruno-fernando-joel-embiid-altercation/ |archive-date=October 11, 2021 |access-date=October 10, 2021 |website=NBA.com}} ===Boston / Maine Celtics (2021–2022)=== On August 7, 2021, Fernando was traded to the [[Boston Celtics]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Sacramento Kings]]. On November 19, 2021, Fernando made his debut with the [[Maine Celtics]] scoring four points and shooting 100% from the field.{{cite web |last=D'Amico |first=Marc |date=August 7, 2021 |title=Celtics Acquire Dunn, Fernando in Three-Team Trade |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-acquire-kris-dunn-bruno-fernando-in-three-team-trade |access-date=November 25, 2024 |work=NBA.com}} ===Houston Rockets (2022–2023)=== On February 10, 2022, the [[Houston Rockets]] acquired Fernando, [[Enes Freedom]] and [[Dennis Schröder]] from the [[Boston Celtics]] in exchange for [[Daniel Theis]].{{cite web |date=February 10, 2022 |title=Celtics Re-Acquire Daniel Theis in Four-Player Deal with Rockets |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-re-acquire-daniel-theis-0 |access-date=November 25, 2024 |work=NBA.com}} On July 26, 2022, Fernando re-signed with the Rockets in a two-way deal.{{Cite web |last=Joshi |first=Hiren |date=July 26, 2022 |title=Rockets Re-Sign Bruno Fernando |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-re-sign-bruno-fernando |access-date=2022-07-26 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} On October 2, the Rockets converted his two-way contract into a four-year, $10.9 million deal.{{Cite web |date=October 2, 2022 |title=Rockets agree to four-year deal with Bruno Fernando |url=https://hoopshype.com/2022/10/02/rockets-agree-to-four-year-deal-with-bruno-fernando |access-date=November 25, 2024 |website=HoopsHype.com |archive-date=November 28, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221128092652/https://hoopshype.com/2022/10/02/rockets-agree-to-four-year-deal-with-bruno-fernando/ |url-status=dead }} On October 19, he had his first start on the team with a seven-point, nine-rebound and seven-assist performance in a 117–107 loss to the [[Atlanta Hawks]].{{Cite web |title=Rockets vs. Hawks - NBA Box Score - October 19, 2022 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore/_/gameId/401468020 |access-date=2022-10-20 |website=ESPN |language=en}} ===Return to Atlanta and College Park (2023–2024)=== On February 9, 2023, Fernando and [[Garrison Mathews]] were traded to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for [[Justin Holiday]], [[Frank Kaminsky]] and two future second-round draft picks.{{cite web|first=Hiren|last=Joshi|title=Rockets Complete Four-Player Trade with Atlanta|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-complete-four-player-trade-with-atlanta|website=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2023|access-date=February 9, 2023}} On July 30, 2024, he was waived by the Hawks.{{cite web|title=Atlanta Hawks Request Waivers on Bruno Fernando|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-request-waivers-on-bruno-fernando|website=NBA.com|date=July 30, 2024|access-date=July 30, 2024}} ===Toronto Raptors (2024–2025)=== On August 4, 2024, Fernando signed with the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web|title=RAPTORS SIGN FERNANDO|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-sign-fernando|website=NBA.com|date=August 4, 2024|access-date=August 4, 2024}} He made 17 appearances (two starts) for Toronto during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 3.4 points, 3.0 rebounds, and 1.1 assists. Fernando was waived by the Raptors on January 7, 2025.{{cite web|title=RAPTORS WAIVE FERNANDO|url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/news/raptors-waive-fernando|website=NBA.com|date=January 7, 2025|access-date=January 7, 2025}} === Real Madrid (2025) === [[File:Bruno Fernando 20 Real Madrid Baloncesto Euroleague 20250206 (6).jpg|thumb|270x270px|Fernando with Real Madrid in 2025]] On January 24, 2025, Fernando signed with [[Real Madrid Baloncesto|Real Madrid]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{cite web|title=Comunicado Oficial: Bruno Fernando|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/es-ES/noticias/club/comunicados/comunicado-oficial-bruno-fernando-24-01-2025|website=RealMadrid.coom.com|date=January 24, 2025|access-date=January 25, 2025|language=Spanish}} ===Partizan (2025–2026)=== On October 26, 2025, Fernando signed with [[KK Partizan|Partizan Mozzart Bet]] of the [[Basketball League of Serbia|Serbian League]] (KLS), [[ABA League]], and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web|title=Bruno Fernando officially signs with Partizan|url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1885860/bruno-fernando-officially-signs-with-partizan/|access-date=November 23, 2025|website=eurohoops.net|language=en}} ===Anadolu Efes (2026–present)=== On July 10, 2026, Fernando signed with [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL).{{Cite web|url=https://www.anadoluefessk.org/tr/news/GwbcVauWdu1apclAXyAfXw==|title=Ailemizin yeni üyesi Bruno Fernando|date=July 10, 2026|website=|publisher=[[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]]|language=tr|access-date=July 10, 2026}} ==National team career== Participating in the 2014 FIBA Under-17 World Championship in [[Dubai]], he averaged 9.1 points, 10.6 rebounds and 2.7 blocks per contest for the Angolan national team. In 2016, Bruno Fernando made his debut with [[Angola men's national basketball team|Angola's men's national team]] and participated in the [[FIBA World Olympic Qualifying Tournament|FIBA Olympic Qualifying Tournament]] in [[Belgrade]].{{Cite web |date=August 31, 2017 |title=Angola set to face endless challenges at FIBA AfroBasket 2017 |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/news/afrobasket-2017-news-angola-set-to-face-endless-challenges-at-fiba-afrobsket-2017 |access-date=November 25, 2024 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}} Averaging 18.3 points, 6.6 boards, 2.1 assists and 1.6 blocks per game, he led Angola to gold at the [[2016 FIBA Africa Under-18 Championship]], while receiving [[Eurobasket.com|Afrobasket.com]] All-African Championships U18 Best Player honors.{{Cite news|url=http://www.afrobasket.com/African-Championships-U18/news/456969/Afrobasket.com-All-African-Championships-U18-Awards-2016|title=EUROBASKET NEWS|work=www.eurobasket.com|access-date=December 30, 2017}} He later also joined the [[Angola men's national basketball team|Angola senior team]] for the 2018 Olympic Qualifiers. He did not play for his country for four years, until returning in August 2022 for Angola's World Cup qualifiers.{{Cite web |date=August 21, 2022 |title=What can the first Angolan in the NBA bring to the table in Window 4? |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/basketballworldcup/2023/african-qualifiers/news/what-can-the-first-angolan-in-the-nba-bring-to-the-table-in-window-4 |access-date=2022-08-23 |website=FIBA.basketball |language=en}} Fernando played at [[FIBA AfroBasket 2025]] and helped Angola win its record-extending twelfth gold medal, and was named to the [[FIBA AfroBasket All-Tournament Team|All-Tournament Team]] in the process.{{Cite web |date=2025-08-24 |title=MVP Dundao headlines 2025 AfroBasket All-Tournament Team |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/fiba-afrobasket-2025/news/mvp-dundao-headlines-2025-afrobasket-all-tournament-team |access-date=2025-08-25 |website=www.fiba.basketball |language=en}}
